Our project: vision safety system for rotating machinery (conveyor end rollers, paper/film rewinder rolls, nip points). One fixed factory CCTV, pretrained pose (RTMPose 17 keypoints, CPU), user-drawn hazard boundary (roll as cylinder), rule-based state machine normal/warning/slow/stop. Ground truth = a human judging every 0.2s 'should the machine stop now?'. Core pain: in 2D, a worker standing in front of or passing by the roll looks overlapping -> false stops; thresholds fit to one video do not transfer (missed 3 of 5 new accident videos); depth models (Depth Anything V2 rel/metric), 3D pose (RTMW3D), roll-axis crossing rule all failed; hand approach-velocity/TTC rule is too late (humans flag danger earlier from approach/walking direction). Now testing: foot ground-plane position (homography from user-drawn floor parallel lines, scale from person height) as gate; but camera calibration from vanishing points failed on 3 of 8 videos (weak perspective/zoomed screen recordings, machine running across the image so one vanishing point is at infinity).

Topic: Foot/ground-plane anchored bird's-eye-view (homography) hazard zone monitoring with a single CCTV: how systems decide 'within reach of the machine', how they handle occluded feet (worker leaning into machine, feet hidden), margins for homography error, results on false alarms.
